_comment: Labeled evaluation set for the RAG pipeline. Canonical source for questions and expectations; human notes and check history live in the private EVAL.md. 'require': 'any' = hit if at least one expected doc is in top-8; 'all' = every listed doc must be found. Articles are identified by url, papers by arxiv_id (version suffix ignored). Questions 8-16 are REAL user questions (owner, 2026-10-31, from the asked_questions log); highlight-to-ask questions keep the exact combined string the chat sends. Time-sensitive questions (marked in _note) need periodic relabeling: their gold answer changes as the corpus grows.

retrieval.question: what is new about exoplanets?
retrieval._note: TIME-SENSITIVE ('new'). Relabeled 2026-10-31: the July 2026 labels went stale on prod (newer exoplanet articles rightly outrank them) — first documented label-rot case. Refresh these periodically.

retrieval.question: aurora forecast and geomagnetic storms
retrieval._note: Relabeled 2026-10-31: the lone July cubesat label failed everywhere (retrieval miss + model refusal agreed it was broken); added NASA COFFIES storm-prediction article as an alternative gold.

retrieval.question: how do coronal mass ejections interact with the solar wind?
what has the Rubin Observatory discovered so far?
can a thermal camera improve gravitational wave detectors?
what is the Einstein Probe?
retrieval._note: Definition-style question (first of its kind in the set). Verified live in the cloud chat 2026-08-25: answer wove together 2 papers + 2 articles.

retrieval.question:
Regarding this passage from the journal: "Crew-13 Blasts Off"

which exactly experiments?
retrieval._note: First REAL highlight-to-ask question (owner, 2026-10-31). 'What You Need to Know' URL corrected 2026-10-31 to the prod spelling (missions/station/commercial-crew), my earlier guess pointed at humans-in-space.

retrieval.question:
Regarding this passage from the journal: "CHARA Array"

Where this telescope is located?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31. Of the three CHARA papers in the corpus only the SPICA abstract names Mount Wilson (checked against arXiv 2026-10-31), so it is the single gold.

retrieval.question: What is the latest information about changes in the size of the universe? Is it expanding?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31. Mildly TIME-SENSITIVE ('latest'), but the dark-energy-debate golds should stay valid for a long while.

retrieval.question: How big is the Lazuli Space Telescope's mirror compared to Hubble's?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31 — the owner asked one of the journal's own suggested questions; the answer (3 m vs 2.4 m) is in this single article.

retrieval.question:
Regarding this passage from the journal: "isolated galaxies lose the gas they need to form stars."

Why that happens?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31. Edge-of-corpus case: the sources cover quenching mechanisms in general, not isolated galaxies specifically, and the live answer honestly said so while citing these four.

retrieval.question: did anyone try to save the Swift telescope?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31. Multi-article narrative (rescue launched -> called off -> lessons learned).

retrieval.question: did the young Sun affect Earth's climate?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31. News + paper synthesis (faint young Sun paradox, superflares, heliosphere).

retrieval.question: why was China's Moon mission postponed?
retrieval._note: Live 2026-10-31. The sources only say 'launch conditions' — the live answer correctly flagged how vague that is.

abstention.question: when will the next total solar eclipse be visible from Ukraine?
abstention._note: Corpus covers 2026/2027 eclipses but nothing about Ukraine visibility: the answer should say it does not know about Ukraine while summarizing what the sources do cover.

abstention.question: what did Elon Musk say about the Mars colony budget this week?
abstention._note: Nothing remotely relevant in the corpus: expect a clean refusal with no sources cited.

abstention.question: what telescope to choose in 2026 for beginner?
abstention._note: Intent-mismatch case: the corpus is full of telescope documents (Roman, LBT, iLocater) so retrieval scores look fine, but they are science news, not buying advice. Expect a refusal that may legitimately cite sources when explaining what the corpus does cover.

abstention.question:
Regarding this passage from the journal: "An AI-powered navigation system called AutoNav"

What's the algorithn behind NASA's Perseverance rover's navigation system Autonav?
abstention._note: REAL question (owner, 2026-10-31, typo kept verbatim). The corpus mentions AutoNav but never explains the algorithm; the live answer correctly refused while citing what the sources do say.

abstention.question:
Regarding this passage from the journal: "Sophie Adenot became the latest European to return from a long-duration mission in what ESA called her 'εpsilon mission.'"

Why it is called like that?
abstention._note: REAL question (owner, 2026-10-31). The mission-name doc exists in the corpus but never explains the name — the cleanest 'source found, answer absent' case we have.
